top_categories.workout_context: Gran Fondo Asociación Española's mixed terrain rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Gran Fondo Asociación Española's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before September.
At mile 60 of 85, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Gran Fondo Asociación Española. Train it until it feels boring.
When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.

Road-specific control matters at Gran Fondo Asociación Española. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 85 miles.
At Gran Fondo Asociación Española, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 85 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
Long rides with hard efforts mixed in. Simulates what Gran Fondo Asociación Española's mixed terrain actually does to you.
2-minute all-out efforts on mixed terrain. Closing gaps, responding to attacks, sprinting for position. Train the burn.

Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Gran Fondo Asociación Española. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 85 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.

race_overlay.weather: September in Montevideo and Canelones Department, Uruguay. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks before Gran Fondo Asociación Española. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Gran Fondo Asociación Española’s 85 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Race Simulation, and Durability to prepare you for 85 miles of mixed terrain in Montevideo and Canelones Department, Uruguay.
